## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) for the absolutely continuous causal-curve
calculus and the supplied causal results used below.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]). Let $C\subseteq M$ be a strictly
convex normal set ([[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]]
clause (b)), let $p\in C$, and write
$$W_p:=\exp_p^{-1}(C)\subseteq T_pM,\qquad v(q):=\exp_p^{-1}(q),\qquad P(p,q):=d(\exp_p)_{v(q)}(v(q)),\qquad D_p^2(q):=g_p(v(q),v(q)).$$
Define
$$J_C^+(p):=\{p\}\cup\{q\in C:\text{there is a future causal curve } \sigma:[0,1]\to C\text{ with }\sigma(0)=p,\ \sigma(1)=q\},$$
so the reflexive endpoint $p$ is included even though a constant curve is
not in the curve class. Define
$$I_C^+(p):=\{q\in C:\text{there is a future timelike curve } \sigma:[0,1]\to C\text{ with }\sigma(0)=p,\ \sigma(1)=q\}$$
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]). Put
$$\mathcal C^+:=\{v\in W_p:v\text{ is future causal or }v=0\},\quad \mathcal T^+:=\{v\in W_p:v\text{ is future timelike}\},\quad \mathcal N^+:=\{v\in W_p:v\text{ is future null and }v\ne0\}.$$
Then:

**(a) Causal containment.** For every future causal curve
$\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ with $\sigma(0)=p$, the position vector
$v(\sigma(t))$ is future causal or zero for every $t\in[0,1]$.

**(b) Cone characterizations.**
$$J^+_C(p)=\exp_p(\mathcal C^+),\qquad I^+_C(p)=\exp_p(\mathcal T^+),\qquad J^+_C(p)\setminus\bigl(I^+_C(p)\cup\{p\}\bigr)=\exp_p(\mathcal N^+).$$

**(c) Null rigidity.** Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be future causal with
$\sigma(0)=p$, and let $\hat s\in(0,1]$ satisfy: $v(\sigma(\hat s))$ is
future null nonzero and $v(\sigma(t))\ne0$ for every $t\in(0,\hat s]$. Then
there are $v_0\in\mathcal N^+$ and a nondecreasing absolutely continuous
surjection $\varphi:[0,\hat s]\to[0,1]$ with
$\sigma(t)=\exp_p(\varphi(t)v_0)$ for $0\le t\le\hat s$.

**(d) Length maximality.** Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be future causal with
$\sigma(0)=p$. Then
$$L_g(\sigma)\le\sqrt{-D_p^2\bigl(\sigma(1)\bigr)}=\sqrt{-g_p\bigl(v(\sigma(1)),v(\sigma(1))\bigr)} .$$
If moreover $v(\sigma(1))$ is future timelike and $v(\sigma(t))\ne0$ for all
$t\in(0,1]$, then equality holds if and only if there are $v_0$ future
timelike and a nondecreasing absolutely continuous surjection
$\varphi:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ with $\sigma(t)=\exp_p(\varphi(t)v_0)$ for all $t$.

## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum with $s>0$ and
$f(r)=1-s/r$ ([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]), with
$f'=s/r^2$. Then:

For arbitrary $x^0_0,\varphi_0\in\mathbb R$, put
$\omega_0=(\cos\varphi_0,\sin\varphi_0,0)\in S^2$. For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$
define the rotation
$$R_\alpha(y_1,y_2,y_3):=(y_1\cos\alpha-y_2\sin\alpha,\ y_1\sin\alpha+y_2\cos\alpha,\ y_3),$$
and the global axial vector field $\Phi(y_1,y_2,y_3):=(-y_2,y_1,0)$ on $S^2$;
it is tangent because $y\cdot\Phi(y)=0$ for $y\in S^2$.
In every spherical-polar chart near the equator, $\Phi=\partial_\varphi$;
longitude expressions below are local chart expressions for the global sphere
curve $R_\alpha\omega_0$.

In this item, a **timelike circular geodesic** means a future timelike
geodesic whose areal radius $r$ is constant on an interval of positive length;
its angular orientation is unrestricted.

**(a) Existence of circular timelike geodesics.** Let $r_0>3s/2$ and choose
$\ell\in\mathbb R$ with

$$\ell^2=\frac{c^2sr_0^2}{2r_0-3s}>0,\qquad e:=\Bigl(f(r_0)\Bigl(c^2+\frac{\ell^2}{r_0^2}\Bigr)\Bigr)^{1/2} =\frac{c(r_0-s)\sqrt 2}{\sqrt{r_0(2r_0-3s)}}>0 .$$

Then the globally defined curve $\gamma:\mathbb R\to M$ is

$$\gamma(\tau):=\bigl(x^0_0+\tfrac{e}{f(r_0)}\tau,\ r_0,\ R_{\ell\tau/r_0^2}\omega_0\bigr).$$
In each local polar chart along it, $\vartheta=\pi/2$ and the longitude is
$\varphi_0+\ell\tau/r_0^2$ up to a constant multiple of $2\pi$.

It is a future timelike geodesic of the datum, with $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-c^2$
and with the conserved quantities $e=-g(\gamma',\partial_0)$ and
$\ell=g(\gamma',\Phi)$ of
[[lem-gr-schwarzschild-timelike-geodesic-reduction]]; it is a **circular
orbit** at radius $r_0$. Its angular velocity in the coordinate $x^0$ is

$$\frac{d\varphi}{dx^0}=\frac{\ell f(r_0)}{r_0^2e}=\operatorname{sgn}(\ell)\Bigl(\frac{s}{2r_0^3}\Bigr)^{1/2},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \Bigl(\frac{d\varphi}{dt}\Bigr)^2=\frac{G_Nm_*}{r_0^3},$$

$t=x^0/c$.

**(b) The circular-orbit condition is necessary.** Conversely, if
$\gamma:I\to M$ is any future timelike geodesic parametrized by proper time with
$r(\tau)\equiv r_0>s$ constant on an interval of positive length, then
$r_0>\frac{3s}{2}$. If $\gamma$ is equatorial, its conserved angular
momentum additionally satisfies $\ell^2=\dfrac{c^2sr_0^2}{2r_0-3s}$.
Consequently no timelike circular geodesic, in any angular orientation, exists
with $s<r_0\le\frac{3s}{2}$.

**(c) Stability threshold of the radial potential.** For each radius
$r>\frac{3s}{2}$ set $\ell_r^2:=c^2sr^2/(2r-3s)$ and regard $\ell_r$ as a
constant in the function $V_{\ell_r}(x):=\tfrac12 f(x)(c^2+\ell_r^2/x^2)$.
Differentiate with respect to $x$ at fixed $\ell_r$, then evaluate at $x=r$.
The result, evaluated at the circular value $\ell_r$, is

$$V_{\ell_r}''(r)=\frac{c^2s(r-3s)}{r^3(2r-3s)},\qquad r>\frac{3s}{2},$$

so $V_\ell$ has a strict local minimum at the circular-orbit radius exactly
for $r>3s$, a strict local maximum exactly for $\frac{3s}{2}<r<3s$, and
$V_\ell''(3s)=0$; the radius $r=3s$ is the **innermost stable circular orbit
radius** of the restricted model in this potential sense.

**(d) The photon sphere at $r=3s/2$.** Let $\ell\neq0$ and put
$r_0=\frac{3s}{2}$ and $e_0:=\dfrac{\lvert\ell\rvert\sqrt{f(r_0)}}{r_0}=\dfrac{2\lvert\ell\rvert}{3\sqrt3\,s}>0$.
Then the globally defined curve
$$\eta(\tau):=\bigl(x^0_0+\tfrac{e_0}{f(r_0)}\tau,\ r_0,\ R_{\ell\tau/r_0^2}\omega_0\bigr),\qquad \tau\in\mathbb R,$$
whose local polar expressions have $\vartheta=\pi/2$ and longitude
$\varphi_0+\ell\tau/r_0^2$ up to chart shifts, is a future null geodesic (a
**null circular orbit** or **photon sphere**
orbit) with conserved quantities $e_0=-g(\eta',\partial_0)$ and
$\ell=g(\eta',\Phi)$, and its angular velocity is

$$\frac{d\varphi}{dx^0}=\frac{\ell f(r_0)}{r_0^2e_0}=\operatorname{sgn}(\ell)\,\frac{\sqrt{f(r_0)}}{r_0},\qquad \Bigl(\frac{d\varphi}{dx^0}\Bigr)^2=\frac{f(r_0)}{r_0^2}=\frac{4}{27s^2}.$$

The **null effective potential** $W^{\mathrm n}_\ell(r):=f(r)\ell^2/r^2$
satisfies $(W^{\mathrm n}_\ell)'(3s/2)=0$ and
$(W^{\mathrm n}_\ell)''(3s/2)=-\dfrac{32\ell^2}{81s^4}<0$, so the photon-sphere
radius is a strict local maximum of the null potential.

**(e) Scope.** All statements are exact data of the restricted model: the
orbits are ideal geodesics of the metric on the exterior domain, the
stability claim is the sign of the second derivative of the stated potential,
and no claim is made about nonlinear stability, about orbital decay, about
observations or about the interior region. The case $r_0=s$ is excluded, and
the reduction is stated only where $r>s$.

$r>\frac{3s}{2}$ set $\ell_r^2:=c^2sr^2/(2r-3s)$ and regard $\ell_r$ as a
constant in the function $V_{\ell_r}(x):=\tfrac12 f(x)(c^2+\ell_r^2/x^2)$.
Differentiate with respect to $x$ at fixed $\ell_r$, then evaluate at $x=r$.
The result, evaluated at the circular value $\ell_r$, is

$$V_{\ell_r}''(r)=\frac{c^2s(r-3s)}{r^3(2r-3s)},\qquad r>\frac{3s}{2},$$

so $V_\ell$ has a strict local minimum at the circular-orbit radius exactly
for $r>3s$, a strict local maximum exactly for $\frac{3s}{2}<r<3s$, and
$V_\ell''(3s)=0$; the radius $r=3s$ is the **innermost stable circular orbit
radius** of the restricted model in this potential sense.

**(d) The photon sphere at $r=3s/2$.** Let $\ell\neq0$ and put
$r_0=\frac{3s}{2}$ and $e_0:=\dfrac{\lvert\ell\rvert\sqrt{f(r_0)}}{r_0}=\dfrac{2\lvert\ell\rvert}{3\sqrt3\,s}>0$.
Then the globally defined curve
$$\eta(\tau):=\bigl(x^0_0+\tfrac{e_0}{f(r_0)}\tau,\ r_0,\ R_{\ell\tau/r_0^2}\omega_0\bigr),\qquad \tau\in\mathbb R,$$
whose local polar expressions have $\vartheta=\pi/2$ and longitude
$\varphi_0+\ell\tau/r_0^2$ up to chart shifts, is a future null geodesic (a
**null circular orbit** or **photon sphere**
orbit) with conserved quantities $e_0=-g(\eta',\partial_0)$ and
$\ell=g(\eta',\Phi)$, and its angular velocity is

$$\frac{d\varphi}{dx^0}=\frac{\ell f(r_0)}{r_0^2e_0}=\operatorname{sgn}(\ell)\,\frac{\sqrt{f(r_0)}}{r_0},\qquad \Bigl(\frac{d\varphi}{dx^0}\Bigr)^2=\frac{f(r_0)}{r_0^2}=\frac{4}{27s^2}.$$

The **null effective potential** $W^{\mathrm n}_\ell(r):=f(r)\ell^2/r^2$
satisfies $(W^{\mathrm n}_\ell)'(3s/2)=0$ and
$(W^{\mathrm n}_\ell)''(3s/2)=-\dfrac{32\ell^2}{81s^4}<0$, so the photon-sphere
radius is a strict local maximum of the null potential.

**(e) Scope.** All statements are exact data of the restricted model: the
orbits are ideal geodesics of the metric on the exterior domain, the
stability claim is the sign of the second derivative of the stated potential,
and no claim is made about nonlinear stability, about orbital decay, about
observations or about the interior region. The case $r_0=s$ is excluded, and
the reduction is stated only where $r>s$.

## Definition

Let $(M,g,N)=(\mathbb R^4,\eta,\partial_0)$ be the flat model with its
inertial chart and let $c>0$ be the parameter of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]. All objects below are
component families in this chart.

**(a) Linearized-wave datum.** Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be a
nonempty open set and let $K\subseteq\Omega$ be a nonempty compact set. Fix a
length scale $L>0$, and use the numerical threshold $\delta_0=1/16$ and
chart control functional $B_K$ defined in
[[pthm-gr-linearized-field-equations]] clause (d) for this $K,L$. A
**linearized-wave datum on $K$** consists of:

- a flat linearized family $(\varepsilon_1,h,q)$ over $\Omega$ with
  perturbation $h$ ([[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]]) such that
  $B_K(h)<\infty$ in the chart control functional of that clause;
- the real cosmological parameter $\Lambda$ and a smooth family
  $\mathcal T(\lambda)$ of stress-energy tensor fields on $\Omega$ for
  $\lambda\in(-\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_1)$, with component fields smooth
  jointly in $(\lambda,x)$ ([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]);
- the zeroth-order compatibility condition
  $\kappa\mathcal T_{ab}(0)=\Lambda\eta_{ab}$, where
  $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$; define the linearized source field, with curvature
  units, by $S_{ab}:=\kappa\,\partial_\lambda\mathcal T_{ab}(\lambda)|_0$,
  and require
  $G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)+\Lambda h_{ab}=S_{ab}$ in the sense of
  [[def-gr-plane-wave-perturbation]] clause (e);
- a nonzero real amplitude $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|<\varepsilon_1$ for
  which $g(\lambda):=\eta+\lambda h$ is a Lorentzian metric of signature
  $(-,+,+,+)$ on a neighborhood of $K$.

The parameter $\lambda$ is dimensionless, and in the adopted SI length
coordinates $S_{ab}$, $G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)$ and $\Lambda h_{ab}$ have units
$\mathrm m^{-2}$, whereas $\mathcal T_{ab}$ has energy-density units and
$\kappa\mathcal T_{ab}$ has units $\mathrm m^{-2}$
([[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]). The $B_K$ and $\delta_0$
values in the chart Taylor estimate are numerical controls: evaluate
component functions and their coordinate derivatives as SI numerical values
in this fixed length-coordinate chart, then form the displayed real-valued
functional. It is not a physical observable or an intrinsic norm. In this
fixed numerical convention, $B_K$, $\delta_0$ and $C_{K,L}$ are real control
numbers and $C_{K,L}B_K^2/L^2$ has the residual component unit
$\mathrm m^{-2}$ for $L$ in metres. The datum is a
**linearized vacuum wave datum** when $S=0$ and $\Lambda=0$. If in addition
the perturbation is a TT planar perturbation with amplitudes $A_+,A_\times$
([[def-gr-plane-wave-perturbation]] clause (b)), the datum is a **TT
linearized-wave datum**. Its **approximation defect** is

$$D(\lambda,K):=\max_{a,b}\ \sup_{p\in K}\bigl|G_{ab}(\eta+\lambda h)(p)+\Lambda\,g_{ab}(\lambda)(p)-\kappa\,\mathcal T_{ab}(\lambda,p)\bigr|,$$

where $G$ is the Einstein tensor of the exact metric $\eta+\lambda h$;
this is the residual against the specified exact stress-energy family, not
against its first-order coefficient alone. In length coordinates it has
units $\mathrm m^{-2}$. The datum is **within the quadratic approximation**
when $|\lambda|B_K(h)\le\delta_0$. This uses the chosen threshold rather than
an unspecified existential $\delta_0/B_K(h)$, and also covers $B_K(h)=0$.
Whether a datum satisfies any of these conditions is a property of the
given data; this definition names the data, the condition and the defect and
asserts neither existence nor a bound.

**(b) Ideal two-body detector.** Let a TT linearized-wave datum be given.
Choose a nonempty open interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$, a spatial point
$x_0\in\mathbb R^3$, and a nonzero spatial vector $\delta\in\mathbb R^3$
with Euclidean norm $|\delta|>0$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Require
the coordinate tube

$$\mathcal A_{J,\delta}:=\{(cs,\,x_0+q\delta):s\in J,\ q\in[0,1]\}$$

to lie in $\Omega$. For $q\in[0,1]$ define the smooth curves
$\gamma_q:J\to\Omega$ by $\gamma_q(s):=(cs,\,x_0+q\delta)$, and require
$g(\lambda)$ to be Lorentzian on a neighborhood of $\mathcal A_{J,\delta}$;
the
**reference worldline** is $\gamma_0$ and the **companion worldline** is
$\gamma_1$. Whenever these endpoint curves are the ideal freely falling
worldlines assigned by the postulate of [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]],
their pair with $(x_0,\delta)$ is the **ideal two-body detector**. Its
**arm direction** is $e_\delta:=\delta/|\delta|$, the spatial unit vector in
the chosen inertial chart.

In SI length coordinates, the components of $x_0$ and $\delta$ and the arm
length $|\delta|$ are in metres, while $e_\delta$ is dimensionless.

**(c) Finite arm length and strain.** For $s\in J$ the prescribed spatial
arm path is $\sigma_s:[0,1]\to\Omega$, $\sigma_s(q):=\gamma_q(s)$, with
tangent $\dot\sigma_s(q)=\delta^i\partial_i$. Its **metric arm length** is
the metric length of this spacelike coordinate segment,

$$L_\delta(s):=\int_0^1\sqrt{g(\lambda)_{\sigma_s(q)}(\dot\sigma_s(q),\dot\sigma_s(q))}\,dq,$$

inertial chart and let $c>0$ be the parameter of

chart control functional $B_K$ defined in
[[pthm-gr-linearized-field-equations]] clause (d) for this $K,L$. A
**linearized-wave datum on $K$** consists of:

  perturbation $h$ ([[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]]) such that

  $\mathcal T(\lambda)$ of stress-energy tensor fields on $\Omega$ for
  $\lambda\in(-\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_1)$, with component fields smooth
  jointly in $(\lambda,x)$ ([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]);

  $\kappa\mathcal T_{ab}(0)=\Lambda\eta_{ab}$, where
  $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$; define the linearized source field, with curvature
  units, by $S_{ab}:=\kappa\,\partial_\lambda\mathcal T_{ab}(\lambda)|_0$,
  and require
  $G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)+\Lambda h_{ab}=S_{ab}$ in the sense of
  [[def-gr-plane-wave-perturbation]] clause (e);
- a nonzero real amplitude $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|<\varepsilon_1$ for
  which $g(\lambda):=\eta+\lambda h$ is a Lorentzian metric of signature
  $(-,+,+,+)$ on a neighborhood of $K$.

coordinates $S_{ab}$, $G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)$ and $\Lambda h_{ab}$ have units

$\kappa\mathcal T_{ab}$ has units $\mathrm m^{-2}$

## Definition

Let $(M,g,N)=(\mathbb R^4,\eta,\partial_0)$ be the flat model with its
inertial chart and let $c>0$ be the parameter of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]. All objects below are
component families in this chart.

**(a) Linearized-wave datum.** Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be a
nonempty open set and let $K\subseteq\Omega$ be a nonempty compact set. Fix a
length scale $L>0$, and use the numerical threshold $\delta_0=1/16$ and
chart control functional $B_K$ defined in
[[pthm-gr-linearized-field-equations]] clause (d) for this $K,L$. A
**linearized-wave datum on $K$** consists of:

- a flat linearized family $(\varepsilon_1,h,q)$ over $\Omega$ with
  perturbation $h$ ([[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]]) such that
  $B_K(h)<\infty$ in the chart control functional of that clause;
- the real cosmological parameter $\Lambda$ and a smooth family
  $\mathcal T(\lambda)$ of stress-energy tensor fields on $\Omega$ for
  $\lambda\in(-\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_1)$, with component fields smooth
  jointly in $(\lambda,x)$ ([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]);
- the zeroth-order compatibility condition
  $\kappa\mathcal T_{ab}(0)=\Lambda\eta_{ab}$, where
  $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$; define the linearized source field, with curvature
  units, by $S_{ab}:=\kappa\,\partial_\lambda\mathcal T_{ab}(\lambda)|_0$,
  and require
  $G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)+\Lambda h_{ab}=S_{ab}$ in the sense of
  [[def-gr-plane-wave-perturbation]] clause (e);
- a nonzero real amplitude $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|<\varepsilon_1$ for
  which $g(\lambda):=\eta+\lambda h$ is a Lorentzian metric of signature
  $(-,+,+,+)$ on a neighborhood of $K$.

The parameter $\lambda$ is dimensionless, and in the adopted SI length
coordinates $S_{ab}$, $G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)$ and $\Lambda h_{ab}$ have units
$\mathrm m^{-2}$, whereas $\mathcal T_{ab}$ has energy-density units and
$\kappa\mathcal T_{ab}$ has units $\mathrm m^{-2}$
([[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]). The $B_K$ and $\delta_0$
values in the chart Taylor estimate are numerical controls: evaluate
component functions and their coordinate derivatives as SI numerical values
in this fixed length-coordinate chart, then form the displayed real-valued
functional. It is not a physical observable or an intrinsic norm. In this
fixed numerical convention, $B_K$, $\delta_0$ and $C_{K,L}$ are real control
numbers and $C_{K,L}B_K^2/L^2$ has the residual component unit
$\mathrm m^{-2}$ for $L$ in metres. The datum is a
**linearized vacuum wave datum** when $S=0$ and $\Lambda=0$. If in addition
the perturbation is a TT planar perturbation with amplitudes $A_+,A_\times$
([[def-gr-plane-wave-perturbation]] clause (b)), the datum is a **TT
linearized-wave datum**. Its **approximation defect** is

$$D(\lambda,K):=\max_{a,b}\ \sup_{p\in K}\bigl|G_{ab}(\eta+\lambda h)(p)+\Lambda\,g_{ab}(\lambda)(p)-\kappa\,\mathcal T_{ab}(\lambda,p)\bigr|,$$

where $G$ is the Einstein tensor of the exact metric $\eta+\lambda h$;
this is the residual against the specified exact stress-energy family, not
against its first-order coefficient alone. In length coordinates it has
units $\mathrm m^{-2}$. The datum is **within the quadratic approximation**
when $|\lambda|B_K(h)\le\delta_0$. This uses the chosen threshold rather than
an unspecified existential $\delta_0/B_K(h)$, and also covers $B_K(h)=0$.
Whether a datum satisfies any of these conditions is a property of the
given data; this definition names the data, the condition and the defect and
asserts neither existence nor a bound.

**(b) Ideal two-body detector.** Let a TT linearized-wave datum be given.
Choose a nonempty open interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$, a spatial point
$x_0\in\mathbb R^3$, and a nonzero spatial vector $\delta\in\mathbb R^3$
with Euclidean norm $|\delta|>0$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Require
the coordinate tube

$$\mathcal A_{J,\delta}:=\{(cs,\,x_0+q\delta):s\in J,\ q\in[0,1]\}$$

to lie in $\Omega$. For $q\in[0,1]$ define the smooth curves
$\gamma_q:J\to\Omega$ by $\gamma_q(s):=(cs,\,x_0+q\delta)$, and require
$g(\lambda)$ to be Lorentzian on a neighborhood of $\mathcal A_{J,\delta}$;
the
**reference worldline** is $\gamma_0$ and the **companion worldline** is
$\gamma_1$. Whenever these endpoint curves are the ideal freely falling

## Definition

Let $(M,g,N)=(\mathbb R^4,\eta,\partial_0)$ be the flat model with its
inertial chart and let $c>0$ be the parameter of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]. All objects below are
component families in this chart.

**(a) Linearized-wave datum.** Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be a
nonempty open set and let $K\subseteq\Omega$ be a nonempty compact set. Fix a
length scale $L>0$, and use the numerical threshold $\delta_0=1/16$ and
chart control functional $B_K$ defined in
[[pthm-gr-linearized-field-equations]] clause (d) for this $K,L$. A
**linearized-wave datum on $K$** consists of:

- a flat linearized family $(\varepsilon_1,h,q)$ over $\Omega$ with
  perturbation $h$ ([[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]]) such that
  $B_K(h)<\infty$ in the chart control functional of that clause;
- the real cosmological parameter $\Lambda$ and a smooth family
  $\mathcal T(\lambda)$ of stress-energy tensor fields on $\Omega$ for
  $\lambda\in(-\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_1)$, with component fields smooth
  jointly in $(\lambda,x)$ ([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]);
- the zeroth-order compatibility condition
  $\kappa\mathcal T_{ab}(0)=\Lambda\eta_{ab}$, where
  $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$; define the linearized source field, with curvature
  units, by $S_{ab}:=\kappa\,\partial_\lambda\mathcal T_{ab}(\lambda)|_0$,
  and require
  $G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)+\Lambda h_{ab}=S_{ab}$ in the sense of
  [[def-gr-plane-wave-perturbation]] clause (e);
- a nonzero real amplitude $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|<\varepsilon_1$ for
  which $g(\lambda):=\eta+\lambda h$ is a Lorentzian metric of signature
  $(-,+,+,+)$ on a neighborhood of $K$.

The parameter $\lambda$ is dimensionless, and in the adopted SI length
coordinates $S_{ab}$, $G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)$ and $\Lambda h_{ab}$ have units
$\mathrm m^{-2}$, whereas $\mathcal T_{ab}$ has energy-density units and
$\kappa\mathcal T_{ab}$ has units $\mathrm m^{-2}$
([[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]). The $B_K$ and $\delta_0$
values in the chart Taylor estimate are numerical controls: evaluate
component functions and their coordinate derivatives as SI numerical values

fixed numerical convention, $B_K$, $\delta_0$ and $C_{K,L}$ are real control
numbers and $C_{K,L}B_K^2/L^2$ has the residual component unit
$\mathrm m^{-2}$ for $L$ in metres. The datum is a
**linearized vacuum wave datum** when $S=0$ and $\Lambda=0$. If in addition
the perturbation is a TT planar perturbation with amplitudes $A_+,A_\times$
([[def-gr-plane-wave-perturbation]] clause (b)), the datum is a **TT
linearized-wave datum**. Its **approximation defect** is

$$D(\lambda,K):=\max_{a,b}\ \sup_{p\in K}\bigl|G_{ab}(\eta+\lambda h)(p)+\Lambda\,g_{ab}(\lambda)(p)-\kappa\,\mathcal T_{ab}(\lambda,p)\bigr|,$$

where $G$ is the Einstein tensor of the exact metric $\eta+\lambda h$;
this is the residual against the specified exact stress-energy family, not
against its first-order coefficient alone. In length coordinates it has
units $\mathrm m^{-2}$. The datum is **within the quadratic approximation**
when $|\lambda|B_K(h)\le\delta_0$. This uses the chosen threshold rather than
an unspecified existential $\delta_0/B_K(h)$, and also covers $B_K(h)=0$.

given data; this definition names the data, the condition and the defect and
asserts neither existence nor a bound.

**reference worldline** is $\gamma_0$ and the **companion worldline** is

$S_\delta$ is dimensionless.

The **first-order strain response** is

$$S^{(1)}_\delta(s):=\left.\partial_\lambda S_\delta(s)\right|_{\lambda=0}=\tfrac12\int_0^1a_\delta(s,q)\,dq,$$

## Statement

Let $V\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ be a connected nonempty open set with global
coordinates $y$, let $(q_{AB})$ be a smooth symmetric matrix of functions on
$V$ with $D_q:=\det(q_{AB})<0$ everywhere, let $r:V\to(0,\infty)$ be smooth
and let $z=\sum_{A,B}q^{AB}\partial_Ar\,\partial_Br$ be nonzero everywhere; let
$M=V\times S^2$ and let $g$ be the warped metric of
[[lem-gr-warped-spherical-christoffel-and-ricci]], whose Ricci tensor is given
there in clause (c) by $\operatorname{Ric}_{AB}=\operatorname{Ric}(q)_{AB}-(2/r)\operatorname{Hess}_{AB}r$,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{Ai}=0$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}=(1-z-r\Delta_qr)\gamma_{ij}$.
Assume the **vacuum condition**

$$\operatorname{Ric}(g)=0\qquad\text{on }M,$$

that is, the vanishing of all components of the Ricci tensor of $g$ in every
product chart. Then:

**(a) Mass parameter.** There is a constant $s\in\mathbb R$ such that
$z=1-\dfrac{s}{r}$ on $V$; equivalently $r(1-z)=s$.

**(b) Local Schwarzschild coordinates.** For every $p\in V$ there are an open
neighborhood $W\subseteq V$ of $p$ and a smooth function $T:W\to\mathbb R$ such
that $(T,r)$ is a smooth coordinate system on $W$, the vector field
$\partial_T$ coincides on $W$ with the volume-form field $K$ of
[[lem-gr-warped-base-vacuum-reduction]], and in these coordinates

$$q=-\Bigl(1-\frac{s}{r}\Bigr)dT\otimes dT+\Bigl(1-\frac{s}{r}\Bigr)^{-1}dr\otimes dr \qquad\text{on }W,$$

where $\bigl(1-s/r\bigr)^{-1}$ is the smooth function $1/z$ on $W$.

**(c) Local Schwarzschild form of the metric.** In the product chart
$(T,r,\vartheta,\varphi)$ over $W\times S^2$ the components of $g$ are

$$g_{TT}=-\Bigl(1-\frac{s}{r}\Bigr),\quad g_{rr}=\Bigl(1-\frac{s}{r}\Bigr)^{-1},\quad g_{\vartheta\vartheta}=r^2,\quad g_{\varphi\varphi}=r^2\sin^2\vartheta,$$

with all mixed components zero; that is,
$g=-\bigl(1-\frac{s}{r}\bigr)dT\otimes dT+\bigl(1-\frac{s}{r}\bigr)^{-1}dr\otimes dr+r^2\gamma_{S^2}$
on the chart domain.

**(d) Extra Killing field.** $\partial_T=K$ is a Killing field of $g$ on the
chart domain in the sense of [[def-gr-killing-field]]; it satisfies
$\partial_T(r)=0$ and $g(\partial_T,\partial_T)=-z=-(1-s/r)$. On a subregion

$z<0$, it is spacelike and no staticity is asserted. In either case it is an
additional symmetry not assumed among the hypotheses.

produced, and $s$ is a constant on the connected set $V$ but need not be
positive, need not be the same for a different connected component of a larger
region, and no asymptotic flatness, regular-center, completeness, maximality or
global uniqueness statement is made. The hypotheses $D_q<0$ and $z\ne0$
are exactly those of the two quoted lemmas, and $r>0$ is used to divide by $r$.

## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), let $p\in M$ and let $U_p=\exp_p(W_p)$
be a normal neighborhood of $p$ with $W_p$ star-shaped, as in
[[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (a). Write
$v(q):=\exp_p^{-1}(q)$ for $q\in U_p$, $P(p,q):=d(\exp_p)_{v(q)}(v(q))$, and
$D_p^2(q):=g_p(v(q),v(q))$.

**(a) Differential in the second argument.** $D_p^2$ is smooth on $U_p$ and,
for every $q\in U_p$ and every $w\in T_qM$,
$$d(D_p^2)_q(w)=2\,g_q\bigl(P(p,q),w\bigr).$$

**(b) Reversal.** Let $q\in U_p$ and let $\gamma:[0,1]\to M$,
$\gamma(t)=\exp_p(t\,v(q))$, be the radial geodesic, so that
$\gamma(1)=q$. Then the reversed segment $t\mapsto\gamma(1-t)$ is the
restriction to $[0,1]$ of the maximal geodesic from $q$ with initial velocity
$-P(p,q)$; consequently
$$\exp_q^{-1}(p)=-P(p,q)\quad\text{and}\quad P(q,p)=-\,v(q)=-(\exp_p)^{-1}(q)$$
whenever the chosen normal inverse at $q$ has a domain containing
$-P(p,q)$ (in particular when $p,q$ lie in one strictly convex normal
set), and then $D^2(q,p)=D^2(p,q)$ by the Gauss
lemma of [[thm-gr-lorentz-gauss-lemma-and-normal-maximum]].

**(c) Differential on pairs in a strictly convex normal set.** If $C$ is a
strictly convex normal set ([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) and
$p,q\in C$, then
$D^2:C\times C\to\mathbb R$ is smooth and for all $u\in T_pM$, $w\in T_qM$,
$$dD^2(p,q)(u,w)=2\,g_p\bigl(P(q,p),u\bigr)+2\,g_q\bigl(P(p,q),w\bigr).$$

## Definition

Work in the reduction conventions of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]: $\gamma$ is the signature
$(+---)$ metric, $U$ the unit future timelike vector $U=n$, $r=\rho c^2$, the
frame $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is $\gamma$-orthonormal with $e_0=U$,
$\gamma(e_i,e_j)=\eta_{ij}$ on spatial pairs, and indices are moved with
$\gamma$.

**(a) Schouten tensor.** The **reduction Schouten tensor** of $\gamma$ is
$$S_{ij}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}-\tfrac16S_\gamma\,\gamma_{ij},$$
where $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $S_\gamma=\gamma^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are
the Ricci tensor and scalar curvature of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). If the dust field equation
$G(\gamma)-\Lambda\gamma=\kappa\,r\,U^\flat\otimes U^\flat$ holds, then
$$S_{ij}=\kappa r\Bigl(U_iU_j-\tfrac13\gamma_{ij}\Bigr)-\tfrac13\Lambda\,\gamma_{ij}.$$
This normalization is fixed so that the standard Kulkarni--Nomizu decomposition
$$R_{ijkl}=C_{ijkl}+\tfrac12\bigl(S_{ik}\gamma_{jl}-S_{il}\gamma_{jk}+S_{jl}\gamma_{ik}-S_{jk}\gamma_{il}\bigr)$$
holds for every metric of dimension four, with $C$ the Weyl tensor
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]); the identity is checked on
constant-curvature metrics in the Remarks.

**(b) Prescribed curvature.** The **prescribed curvature tensor** of a
configuration $(C,E,B,r)$ is the tensor field with frame components
$$R^{\mathrm{pre}}{}_{ijkl}:=C_{ijkl}+\tfrac12\bigl(S_{ik}\gamma_{jl}-S_{il}\gamma_{jk}+S_{jl}\gamma_{ik}-S_{jk}\gamma_{il}\bigr),\qquad S_{ij}\text{ as in (a)} ,$$
where $C=C[E,B]$ is the Weyl tensor reconstructed from the electric and
magnetic variables in (d). A **tentative reduced configuration** is a smooth assignment
$(e_a{}^\mu,\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j,E_{ij},B_{ij},r)$ in the gauge of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]. Equality of its actual curvature
with $R^{\mathrm{pre}}$ is the curvature constraint, rather than an assumption
on the independent unknowns. Reduced evolution enforces its time components;
the residual theorem establishes the remaining components from constrained
initial data. This distinction keeps the tentative connection available before
torsion-freeness and the full curvature constraint are proved.

**(c) Electric and magnetic Weyl variables.** For a smooth Weyl-type tensor $C$
of type $(0,4)$ with the curvature symmetries write
$C^*{}_{ijkl}:=\tfrac12C_{ij}{}^{pq}\epsilon_{klpq}$ for its right dual
([[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] clause (c) for
$\epsilon_{ijkl}$). The **electric and magnetic parts with respect to $U$** are
the spatial fields
$$E_{ij}:=C_{0i0j},\qquad B_{ij}:=C^*{}_{0i0j},$$
with frame indices; they are symmetric and spatial in all indices and
trace-free with respect to $h$ whenever $C$ has the Weyl symmetries.

**(d) Reconstruction formula.** Define the dependent tensor
$$C_{ijkl}:=2\bigl(l_{j[k}E_{l]i}-l_{i[k}E_{l]j}\bigr)-2\bigl(U_{[k}B_{l]p}\epsilon^p{}_{ij}+U_{[i}B_{j]p}\epsilon^p{}_{kl}\bigr),$$
with brackets of weight $\tfrac12$ and $l_{ij}=h_{ij}-U_iU_j$; this expression
is the **reconstruction** of a Weyl tensor from a pair $(E,B)$ of symmetric
spatial trace-free fields. The verification that the reconstructed tensor has
the curvature antisymmetries, pair symmetry, cyclic identity and zero traces —
and that its electric and magnetic parts recover $(E,B)$ — is the content of
[[lem-gr-dust-weyl-reconstruction-from-electric-magnetic]].

The definition fixes the objects and conventions only; the evolution and
subsidiary equations, the initial-data determination and the local existence
theorem are proved in the items named above and in
[[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]] and
[[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]].

Its action on a four-manifold is smooth when each $p\mapsto n\cdot p$ is smooth; a smooth action and freeness and properness are as in [[def-group-action]] and [[def-free-and-proper-lie-group-actions]]: free means trivial stabilizers, proper means the action-graph map $\Theta(n,p)=(n\cdot p,p)$ has compact preimages of compact sets.

## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum with Schwarzschild radius
$s>0$ and $f(r)=1-s/r$
([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]). Let
$M_{\mathrm{ext}}:=\mathbb R\times(0,\infty)\times S^2$ carry the product
smooth structure and let $\iota_{\mathrm{ext}}:M_{\mathrm{ext}}\to S^2$ be the
third projection. Its product atlas includes ordinary sphere charts at the
poles ([[prop-products-of-smooth-manifolds-have-a-canonical-product-smooth-structure]]).
Define the **tortoise function**

$$r_*(r):=r+s\log\left|\frac{r}{s}-1\right|,\qquad r>0,\ r\ne s,$$

on each of the two intervals $(0,s)$ and $(s,\infty)$, and define the
**advanced-chart metric** globally on $M_{\mathrm{ext}}$ by

$$g_{\mathrm{ext}}=-f(r)\,dv\otimes dv+dv\otimes dr+dr\otimes dv+r^2\,\iota_{\mathrm{ext}}^*\gamma_{S^2}.$$

In spherical-polar product charts its components are

$$g_{\mathrm{ext}}=-f(r)\,dv^2+2\,dv\,dr+r^2\,d\Omega^2,$$

namely $g_{vv}=-f$, $g_{vr}=g_{rv}=1$,
$g_{\vartheta\vartheta}=r^2$, $g_{\varphi\varphi}=r^2\sin^2\vartheta$ and all
other components zero. In another sphere chart the angular block is
$r^2(\gamma_{ij})$. Then:

**(a) Smooth Lorentzian metric.** $g_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is a smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field on $M_{\mathrm{ext}}$, and at every point it is
nondegenerate with inertia $(3,1,0)$; hence $(M_{\mathrm{ext}},g_{\mathrm{ext}})$
is a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on all of
$r>0$, including $r=s$.

**(b) Time orientation.** The smooth vector field

$$N_{\mathrm{ext}}:=A(r)\,\partial_v-\partial_r,\qquad A(r):=\frac{f(r)+\sqrt{f(r)^2+4}}{2}>0,$$

satisfies $g_{\mathrm{ext}}(N_{\mathrm{ext}},N_{\mathrm{ext}})<0$ everywhere
and $g_{\mathrm{ext}}(N_{\mathrm{ext}},\partial_v)<0$ everywhere; hence
$N_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is a time orientation of $g_{\mathrm{ext}}$, and on the
region $r>s$ it determines the same future cone as the datum's time
orientation $\partial_v=\partial_0$.

**(c) Isometric embedding of the exterior.** The map
$\Phi:M\to M_{\mathrm{ext}}$, $(x^0,r,\omega)\mapsto(x^0+r_*(r),r,\omega)$
restricts to a diffeomorphism of $M$ onto the open subset $\{r>s\}$ of
$M_{\mathrm{ext}}$, and $\Phi^*g_{\mathrm{ext}}=g$; the exterior datum is
therefore isometric to the region $r>s$ of the extension.

**(d) Vacuum and Kretschmann scalar of the extension.** The
metric-selected connection of $g_{\mathrm{ext}}$ exists and is unique, its
Ricci tensor, scalar curvature and Einstein tensor vanish identically on
$M_{\mathrm{ext}}$, and its Kretschmann scalar equals

$$R_{abcd}R^{abcd}=\frac{12s^2}{r^6}$$

on all of $M_{\mathrm{ext}}$. In particular the scalar is smooth and finite on
the horizon $r=s$, where it takes the value $12/s^4$.

**(e) The horizon is a null hypersurface.** The level set $\{r=s\}$ is a
smooth null hypersurface of $(M_{\mathrm{ext}},g_{\mathrm{ext}})$ whose null
generator direction is $\partial_v$; every smooth product-chart frame remains
a basis across $r=s$. In spherical-polar charts
$\det(g_{\mathrm{ext}})=-r^4\sin^2\vartheta$; in an arbitrary sphere chart
the determinant is $-r^4\det(\gamma_{ij})$, which is nonzero.

**(f) Scope.** The extension constructed here is a smooth Lorentzian
manifold containing the exterior isometrically and regular across $r=s$; it
is not claimed to be maximal, and no uniqueness or global structure theorem
is asserted. The region $r\le0$ and the surfaces relevant to the Kruskal
model of this page are outside this statement.

$$g_{\mathrm{ext}}=-f(r)\,dv^2+2\,dv\,dr+r^2\,d\Omega^2,$$

namely $g_{vv}=-f$, $g_{vr}=g_{rv}=1$,
$g_{\vartheta\vartheta}=r^2$, $g_{\varphi\varphi}=r^2\sin^2\vartheta$ and all
other components zero. In another sphere chart the angular block is
$r^2(\gamma_{ij})$. Then:

covariant $2$-tensor field on $M_{\mathrm{ext}}$, and at every point it is
nondegenerate with inertia $(3,1,0)$; hence $(M_{\mathrm{ext}},g_{\mathrm{ext}})$
is a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on all of
$r>0$, including $r=s$.

**(b) Time orientation.** The smooth vector field

$$N_{\mathrm{ext}}:=A(r)\,\partial_v-\partial_r,\qquad A(r):=\frac{f(r)+\sqrt{f(r)^2+4}}{2}>0,$$

satisfies $g_{\mathrm{ext}}(N_{\mathrm{ext}},N_{\mathrm{ext}})<0$ everywhere
and $g_{\mathrm{ext}}(N_{\mathrm{ext}},\partial_v)<0$ everywhere; hence
$N_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is a time orientation of $g_{\mathrm{ext}}$, and on the
region $r>s$ it determines the same future cone as the datum's time
orientation $\partial_v=\partial_0$.

$\Phi:M\to M_{\mathrm{ext}}$, $(x^0,r,\omega)\mapsto(x^0+r_*(r),r,\omega)$
restricts to a diffeomorphism of $M$ onto the open subset $\{r>s\}$ of
$M_{\mathrm{ext}}$, and $\Phi^*g_{\mathrm{ext}}=g$; the exterior datum is
therefore isometric to the region $r>s$ of the extension.

metric-selected connection of $g_{\mathrm{ext}}$ exists and is unique, its
Ricci tensor, scalar curvature and Einstein tensor vanish identically on
$M_{\mathrm{ext}}$, and its Kretschmann scalar equals

$$R_{abcd}R^{abcd}=\frac{12s^2}{r^6}$$

on all of $M_{\mathrm{ext}}$. In particular the scalar is smooth and finite on
the horizon $r=s$, where it takes the value $12/s^4$.

smooth null hypersurface of $(M_{\mathrm{ext}},g_{\mathrm{ext}})$ whose null

a basis across $r=s$. In spherical-polar charts

the determinant is $-r^4\det(\gamma_{ij})$, which is nonzero.

is not claimed to be maximal, and no uniqueness or global structure theorem
is asserted. The region $r\le0$ and the surfaces relevant to the Kruskal

## Statement

Let $\mathcal K=\{(U,V):UV<1\}\times S^2$, $r$, $g_{\mathcal K}$ and
$N_{\mathcal K}=\partial_U+\partial_V$ be the Kruskal model datum of mass
parameter $m_*$ and Schwarzschild radius $s=2G_Nm_*/c^2>0$
([[def-gr-kruskal-model-data]]). Then:

**(a) The radial function.** The function
$\varphi(r):=-(r/s-1)e^{r/s}$ is a smooth strictly decreasing bijection of
$(0,\infty)$ onto $(-\infty,1)$ with
$\varphi'(r)=-\frac{r}{s^2}e^{r/s}<0$; consequently the relation
$\varphi(r(U,V))=UV$ defines exactly one function
$r:\mathcal K\to(0,\infty)$, and this function is smooth. Moreover
$r(p)=s$ exactly when $U(p)V(p)=0$, and $r(p)\to0$ corresponds to
$U(p)V(p)\to1$; the value $r=0$ is not attained on $\mathcal K$.

**(b) Lorentzian metric and time orientation.**
$g_{\mathcal K}$ is the global smooth tensor of [L1] and is nondegenerate with
inertia $(3,1,0)$ at every point; hence
$(\mathcal K,g_{\mathcal K})$ is a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of
signature $(-,+,+,+)$. The field $N_{\mathcal K}=\partial_U+\partial_V$
satisfies $g_{\mathcal K}(N_{\mathcal K},N_{\mathcal K})=-\frac{4s^3}{r}e^{-r/s}<0$
and is a time orientation.

**(c) The four regions and the isometries.** The set $\{UV\ne0\}$ has four
connected components. Let $r_*$ be the tortoise function of
[[lem-gr-schwarzschild-extension-chart]] on the branch $r>s$ and define
$\Psi_+:M\to\mathcal K$ by
$\Psi_+(x^0,r,\omega)=\bigl(-e^{-(x^0-r_*(r))/(2s)},\,e^{(x^0+r_*(r))/(2s)},\,\omega\bigr)$.
Then $\Psi_+$ is a diffeomorphism of the exterior datum onto the component
$\{U<0,\ V>0\}$ and $\Psi_+^*g_{\mathcal K}=g$. Similarly, on the branch
$0<r<s$ with $r_*=r+s\log(1-r/s)$ the map
$\Psi_-(x^0,r,\omega)=\bigl(e^{(r_*(r)-x^0)/(2s)},\,e^{(r_*(r)+x^0)/(2s)},\,\omega\bigr)$
is a diffeomorphism of the domain $\mathbb R\times(0,s)\times S^2$ (carrying
the metric $-f\,d(x^0)^2+f^{-1}dr^2+r^2\gamma_{S^2}$ with $f<0$) onto the
component $\{U>0,\ V>0\}$ and pulls $g_{\mathcal K}$ back to that metric. The
map $(U,V,\omega)\mapsto(-U,-V,\omega)$ is an isometry of $g_{\mathcal K}$
fixing $r$, exchanging the components $\{U<0,V>0\}\leftrightarrow\{U>0,V<0\}$
and $\{U>0,V>0\}\leftrightarrow\{U<0,V<0\}$; hence every component of
$\{UV\ne0\}$ is isometric to one of the two branches
$-f\,d(x^0)^2+f^{-1}dr^2+r^2d\Omega^2$ with $f=1-s/r$.

**(d) Vacuum and Kretschmann scalar.** The metric-selected connection of
$g_{\mathcal K}$ exists and is unique; its Ricci tensor, scalar curvature and
Einstein tensor vanish identically on $\mathcal K$, and its Kretschmann
scalar equals $R_{abcd}R^{abcd}=12s^2/r^6$ at every point of $\mathcal K$. In
particular the curvature invariant is smooth on $\mathcal K$ and grows
without bound as $UV\to1$ (that is, as $r\downarrow0$ at fixed angles), while
it equals $12/s^4$ on the axes $r=s$.

**(e) Scope.** The statements are geometric. No maximality of the extension,
no geodesic completeness, no uniqueness theorem and no global causal
statement beyond those proved here are asserted. The manifold
$\mathcal K$ contains a copy of the exterior datum and, on the components
with $UV>0$, points at $0<r<s$; the set $\{UV=1\}$ is not part of
$\mathcal K$.

## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum of mass parameter $m_*$,
Schwarzschild radius $s=2G_Nm_*/c^2$ and $f(r)=1-s/r$
([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]), with curvature data as in
[[lem-gr-schwarzschild-ricci-and-einstein-tensors]]. On each spherical-polar
product chart $(x^0,r,\vartheta,\varphi)$ define the local frame field

$$e_{\hat0}:=f^{-1/2}\partial_0,\qquad e_{\hat1}:=f^{1/2}\partial_1,\qquad e_{\hat2}:=r^{-1}\partial_2,\qquad e_{\hat3}:=(r\sin\vartheta)^{-1}\partial_3,$$

and for the curvature tensor define the **frame components**

$$\hat R_{\hat a\hat b\hat c\hat d}:=g\bigl(R(e_{\hat c},e_{\hat d})e_{\hat b},e_{\hat a}\bigr).$$

Then:

**(a) The frame field.** $(e_{\hat0},e_{\hat1},e_{\hat2},e_{\hat3})$ is a
smooth $g$-orthonormal frame (tetrad field) on the chart domain, with
$g(e_{\hat a},e_{\hat b})=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{\hat a\hat b}$, and
$e_{\hat0}$ is future-directed timelike; it is a tetrad field in the sense of
[[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. It is not a coordinate frame.

**(b) Frame components.** The nonzero frame components, up to the
symmetries $R_{abcd}=-R_{bacd}=-R_{abdc}=R_{cdab}$ of
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]], are

$$\hat R_{\hat0\hat1\hat0\hat1}=\frac{f''}{2},\qquad \hat R_{\hat0\hat2\hat0\hat2}=\hat R_{\hat0\hat3\hat0\hat3}=\frac{f'}{2r},$$

$$\hat R_{\hat1\hat2\hat1\hat2}=\hat R_{\hat1\hat3\hat1\hat3}=-\frac{f'}{2r},\qquad \hat R_{\hat2\hat3\hat2\hat3}=\frac{1-f}{r^2},$$

with $f'=s/r^2$ and $f''=-2s/r^3$; all other frame components vanish.

**(c) Kretschmann scalar.** Define the global smooth scalar field
$K:=R_{abcd}R^{abcd}$, with indices raised by the inverse metric. On the
spherical-polar chart locus its component expression is

$$K=f''^2+\frac{4(f')^2}{r^2}+\frac{4(1-f)^2}{r^4},$$

and for the model function $f=1-s/r$ this is

$$K=\frac{12s^2}{r^6}=\frac{48\,G_N^2m_*^2}{c^4\,r^6}.$$

The scalar identity is first computed on the regular angular locus and holds
on all of $M$ by smoothness and density. Since $r>s$ on $M$, one has
$0<K=12s^2/r^6<12/s^4$ at every point; as $r\downarrow s$ the expression has
the finite boundary value $12/s^4$, and the expression $12s^2/r^6$, read as a
function of $r>0$, grows without bound as $r\downarrow0$.

**(d) Scope.** The lemma computes curvature data of the exterior datum on
$r>s$. The limit $r\downarrow s$ is the boundary value on $M$ of the smooth

## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum of mass parameter $m_*$,
Schwarzschild radius $s=2G_Nm_*/c^2$ and $f(r)=1-s/r$
([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]), with curvature data as in
[[lem-gr-schwarzschild-ricci-and-einstein-tensors]]. On each spherical-polar
product chart $(x^0,r,\vartheta,\varphi)$ define the local frame field

$$e_{\hat0}:=f^{-1/2}\partial_0,\qquad e_{\hat1}:=f^{1/2}\partial_1,\qquad e_{\hat2}:=r^{-1}\partial_2,\qquad e_{\hat3}:=(r\sin\vartheta)^{-1}\partial_3,$$

and for the curvature tensor define the **frame components**

$$\hat R_{\hat a\hat b\hat c\hat d}:=g\bigl(R(e_{\hat c},e_{\hat d})e_{\hat b},e_{\hat a}\bigr).$$

Then:

**(a) The frame field.** $(e_{\hat0},e_{\hat1},e_{\hat2},e_{\hat3})$ is a
smooth $g$-orthonormal frame (tetrad field) on the chart domain, with
$g(e_{\hat a},e_{\hat b})=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{\hat a\hat b}$, and
$e_{\hat0}$ is future-directed timelike; it is a tetrad field in the sense of
[[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. It is not a coordinate frame.

**(b) Frame components.** The nonzero frame components, up to the
symmetries $R_{abcd}=-R_{bacd}=-R_{abdc}=R_{cdab}$ of
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]], are

$$\hat R_{\hat0\hat1\hat0\hat1}=\frac{f''}{2},\qquad \hat R_{\hat0\hat2\hat0\hat2}=\hat R_{\hat0\hat3\hat0\hat3}=\frac{f'}{2r},$$

$$\hat R_{\hat1\hat2\hat1\hat2}=\hat R_{\hat1\hat3\hat1\hat3}=-\frac{f'}{2r},\qquad \hat R_{\hat2\hat3\hat2\hat3}=\frac{1-f}{r^2},$$

with $f'=s/r^2$ and $f''=-2s/r^3$; all other frame components vanish.

**(c) Kretschmann scalar.** Define the global smooth scalar field
$K:=R_{abcd}R^{abcd}$, with indices raised by the inverse metric. On the
spherical-polar chart locus its component expression is

$$K=f''^2+\frac{4(f')^2}{r^2}+\frac{4(1-f)^2}{r^4},$$

and for the model function $f=1-s/r$ this is

$$K=\frac{12s^2}{r^6}=\frac{48\,G_N^2m_*^2}{c^4\,r^6}.$$

The scalar identity is first computed on the regular angular locus and holds
on all of $M$ by smoothness and density. Since $r>s$ on $M$, one has
$0<K=12s^2/r^6<12/s^4$ at every point; as $r\downarrow s$ the expression has
the finite boundary value $12/s^4$, and the expression $12s^2/r^6$, read as a
function of $r>0$, grows without bound as $r\downarrow0$.

**(d) Scope.** The lemma computes curvature data of the exterior datum on
$r>s$. The limit $r\downarrow s$ is the boundary value on $M$ of the smooth
expression $12s^2/r^6$; no value of the metric at $r=s$ or at $r=0$ is used
or asserted here, those regions being outside the datum (the regular
continuation across $r=s$ is the separate extension lemma of this page).

## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum with $s>0$ and
$f(r)=1-s/r$ ([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]), with
$f'=s/r^2$. Then:

For arbitrary $x^0_0,\varphi_0\in\mathbb R$, put
$\omega_0=(\cos\varphi_0,\sin\varphi_0,0)\in S^2$. For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$
define the rotation
$$R_\alpha(y_1,y_2,y_3):=(y_1\cos\alpha-y_2\sin\alpha,\ y_1\sin\alpha+y_2\cos\alpha,\ y_3),$$
and the global axial vector field $\Phi(y_1,y_2,y_3):=(-y_2,y_1,0)$ on $S^2$;
it is tangent because $y\cdot\Phi(y)=0$ for $y\in S^2$.
In every spherical-polar chart near the equator, $\Phi=\partial_\varphi$;
longitude expressions below are local chart expressions for the global sphere
curve $R_\alpha\omega_0$.

In this item, a **timelike circular geodesic** means a future timelike
geodesic whose areal radius $r$ is constant on an interval of positive length;
its angular orientation is unrestricted.

**(a) Existence of circular timelike geodesics.** Let $r_0>3s/2$ and choose
$\ell\in\mathbb R$ with

$$\ell^2=\frac{c^2sr_0^2}{2r_0-3s}>0,\qquad e:=\Bigl(f(r_0)\Bigl(c^2+\frac{\ell^2}{r_0^2}\Bigr)\Bigr)^{1/2} =\frac{c(r_0-s)\sqrt 2}{\sqrt{r_0(2r_0-3s)}}>0 .$$

Then the globally defined curve $\gamma:\mathbb R\to M$ is

$$\gamma(\tau):=\bigl(x^0_0+\tfrac{e}{f(r_0)}\tau,\ r_0,\ R_{\ell\tau/r_0^2}\omega_0\bigr).$$
In each local polar chart along it, $\vartheta=\pi/2$ and the longitude is
$\varphi_0+\ell\tau/r_0^2$ up to a constant multiple of $2\pi$.

It is a future timelike geodesic of the datum, with $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-c^2$
and with the conserved quantities $e=-g(\gamma',\partial_0)$ and
$\ell=g(\gamma',\Phi)$ of
[[lem-gr-schwarzschild-timelike-geodesic-reduction]]; it is a **circular
orbit** at radius $r_0$. Its angular velocity in the coordinate $x^0$ is

$$\frac{d\varphi}{dx^0}=\frac{\ell f(r_0)}{r_0^2e}=\operatorname{sgn}(\ell)\Bigl(\frac{s}{2r_0^3}\Bigr)^{1/2},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \Bigl(\frac{d\varphi}{dt}\Bigr)^2=\frac{G_Nm_*}{r_0^3},$$

$t=x^0/c$.

**(b) The circular-orbit condition is necessary.** Conversely, if
$\gamma:I\to M$ is any future timelike geodesic parametrized by proper time with
$r(\tau)\equiv r_0>s$ constant on an interval of positive length, then
$r_0>\frac{3s}{2}$. If $\gamma$ is equatorial, its conserved angular
momentum additionally satisfies $\ell^2=\dfrac{c^2sr_0^2}{2r_0-3s}$.
Consequently no timelike circular geodesic, in any angular orientation, exists
with $s<r_0\le\frac{3s}{2}$.

**(c) Stability threshold of the radial potential.** For each radius
$r>\frac{3s}{2}$ set $\ell_r^2:=c^2sr^2/(2r-3s)$ and regard $\ell_r$ as a
constant in the function $V_{\ell_r}(x):=\tfrac12 f(x)(c^2+\ell_r^2/x^2)$.
Differentiate with respect to $x$ at fixed $\ell_r$, then evaluate at $x=r$.
The result, evaluated at the circular value $\ell_r$, is

$$V_{\ell_r}''(r)=\frac{c^2s(r-3s)}{r^3(2r-3s)},\qquad r>\frac{3s}{2},$$

so $V_\ell$ has a strict local minimum at the circular-orbit radius exactly
for $r>3s$, a strict local maximum exactly for $\frac{3s}{2}<r<3s$, and
$V_\ell''(3s)=0$; the radius $r=3s$ is the **innermost stable circular orbit
radius** of the restricted model in this potential sense.

**(d) The photon sphere at $r=3s/2$.** Let $\ell\neq0$ and put
$r_0=\frac{3s}{2}$ and $e_0:=\dfrac{\lvert\ell\rvert\sqrt{f(r_0)}}{r_0}=\dfrac{2\lvert\ell\rvert}{3\sqrt3\,s}>0$.
Then the globally defined curve
$$\eta(\tau):=\bigl(x^0_0+\tfrac{e_0}{f(r_0)}\tau,\ r_0,\ R_{\ell\tau/r_0^2}\omega_0\bigr),\qquad \tau\in\mathbb R,$$
whose local polar expressions have $\vartheta=\pi/2$ and longitude
$\varphi_0+\ell\tau/r_0^2$ up to chart shifts, is a future null geodesic (a
**null circular orbit** or **photon sphere**
orbit) with conserved quantities $e_0=-g(\eta',\partial_0)$ and
$\ell=g(\eta',\Phi)$, and its angular velocity is

$$\frac{d\varphi}{dx^0}=\frac{\ell f(r_0)}{r_0^2e_0}=\operatorname{sgn}(\ell)\,\frac{\sqrt{f(r_0)}}{r_0},\qquad \Bigl(\frac{d\varphi}{dx^0}\Bigr)^2=\frac{f(r_0)}{r_0^2}=\frac{4}{27s^2}.$$

The **null effective potential** $W^{\mathrm n}_\ell(r):=f(r)\ell^2/r^2$
satisfies $(W^{\mathrm n}_\ell)'(3s/2)=0$ and
$(W^{\mathrm n}_\ell)''(3s/2)=-\dfrac{32\ell^2}{81s^4}<0$, so the photon-sphere
radius is a strict local maximum of the null potential.

**(e) Scope.** All statements are exact data of the restricted model: the
orbits are ideal geodesics of the metric on the exterior domain, the
stability claim is the sign of the second derivative of the stated potential,
and no claim is made about nonlinear stability, about orbital decay, about
observations or about the interior region. The case $r_0=s$ is excluded, and
the reduction is stated only where $r>s$.

$$\ell^2=\frac{c^2sr_0^2}{2r_0-3s}>0,\qquad e:=\Bigl(f(r_0)\Bigl(c^2+\frac{\ell^2}{r_0^2}\Bigr)\Bigr)^{1/2} =\frac{c(r_0-s)\sqrt 2}{\sqrt{r_0(2r_0-3s)}}>0 .$$

Then the globally defined curve $\gamma:\mathbb R\to M$ is

$$\gamma(\tau):=\bigl(x^0_0+\tfrac{e}{f(r_0)}\tau,\ r_0,\ R_{\ell\tau/r_0^2}\omega_0\bigr).$$
In each local polar chart along it, $\vartheta=\pi/2$ and the longitude is
$\varphi_0+\ell\tau/r_0^2$ up to a constant multiple of $2\pi$.

It is a future timelike geodesic of the datum, with $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-c^2$
and with the conserved quantities $e=-g(\gamma',\partial_0)$ and
$\ell=g(\gamma',\Phi)$ of
[[lem-gr-schwarzschild-timelike-geodesic-reduction]]; it is a **circular
orbit** at radius $r_0$. Its angular velocity in the coordinate $x^0$ is

$$\frac{d\varphi}{dx^0}=\frac{\ell f(r_0)}{r_0^2e}=\operatorname{sgn}(\ell)\Bigl(\frac{s}{2r_0^3}\Bigr)^{1/2},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \Bigl(\frac{d\varphi}{dt}\Bigr)^2=\frac{G_Nm_*}{r_0^3},$$

$t=x^0/c$.

**(b) The circular-orbit condition is necessary.** Conversely, if
$\gamma:I\to M$ is any future timelike geodesic parametrized by proper time with
$r(\tau)\equiv r_0>s$ constant on an interval of positive length, then
$r_0>\frac{3s}{2}$. If $\gamma$ is equatorial, its conserved angular
momentum additionally satisfies $\ell^2=\dfrac{c^2sr_0^2}{2r_0-3s}$.
Consequently no timelike circular geodesic, in any angular orientation, exists
with $s<r_0\le\frac{3s}{2}$.

**(c) Stability threshold of the radial potential.** For each radius
$r>\frac{3s}{2}$ set $\ell_r^2:=c^2sr^2/(2r-3s)$ and regard $\ell_r$ as a
constant in the function $V_{\ell_r}(x):=\tfrac12 f(x)(c^2+\ell_r^2/x^2)$.
Differentiate with respect to $x$ at fixed $\ell_r$, then evaluate at $x=r$.
The result, evaluated at the circular value $\ell_r$, is

$$V_{\ell_r}''(r)=\frac{c^2s(r-3s)}{r^3(2r-3s)},\qquad r>\frac{3s}{2},$$

so $V_\ell$ has a strict local minimum at the circular-orbit radius exactly
for $r>3s$, a strict local maximum exactly for $\frac{3s}{2}<r<3s$, and
$V_\ell''(3s)=0$; the radius $r=3s$ is the **innermost stable circular orbit
radius** of the restricted model in this potential sense.

**(d) The photon sphere at $r=3s/2$.** Let $\ell\neq0$ and put
$r_0=\frac{3s}{2}$ and $e_0:=\dfrac{\lvert\ell\rvert\sqrt{f(r_0)}}{r_0}=\dfrac{2\lvert\ell\rvert}{3\sqrt3\,s}>0$.
Then the globally defined curve
$$\eta(\tau):=\bigl(x^0_0+\tfrac{e_0}{f(r_0)}\tau,\ r_0,\ R_{\ell\tau/r_0^2}\omega_0\bigr),\qquad \tau\in\mathbb R,$$
whose local polar expressions have $\vartheta=\pi/2$ and longitude
$\varphi_0+\ell\tau/r_0^2$ up to chart shifts, is a future null geodesic (a
**null circular orbit** or **photon sphere**
orbit) with conserved quantities $e_0=-g(\eta',\partial_0)$ and
$\ell=g(\eta',\Phi)$, and its angular velocity is

$$\frac{d\varphi}{dx^0}=\frac{\ell f(r_0)}{r_0^2e_0}=\operatorname{sgn}(\ell)\,\frac{\sqrt{f(r_0)}}{r_0},\qquad \Bigl(\frac{d\varphi}{dx^0}\Bigr)^2=\frac{f(r_0)}{r_0^2}=\frac{4}{27s^2}.$$

The **null effective potential** $W^{\mathrm n}_\ell(r):=f(r)\ell^2/r^2$
satisfies $(W^{\mathrm n}_\ell)'(3s/2)=0$ and
$(W^{\mathrm n}_\ell)''(3s/2)=-\dfrac{32\ell^2}{81s^4}<0$, so the photon-sphere
radius is a strict local maximum of the null potential.

**(e) Scope.** All statements are exact data of the restricted model: the
orbits are ideal geodesics of the metric on the exterior domain, the
stability claim is the sign of the second derivative of the stated potential,
and no claim is made about nonlinear stability, about orbital decay, about
observations or about the interior region. The case $r_0=s$ is excluded, and
the reduction is stated only where $r>s$.

## Statement

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause
(a), with $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$ and $\Sigma':=j'(\Sigma)$. Let
$\varphi:M\to M'$ be a smooth map with $\varphi^*(g')=g$, with
$g'_{\varphi(p)}(d\varphi_pN_p,N'_{\varphi(p)})<0$ for every $p\in M$, with
$\varphi\circ j=j'$ and $\varphi^*\psi'=\psi$ (so $\varphi$ is a future isometric immersion fixing the complete data and matching every matter field).
Then:

**(a)** $d\varphi_p:T_pM\to T_{\varphi(p)}M'$ is an isomorphism for every
$p\in M$;

**(b)** $\varphi$ is injective, hence a diffeomorphism onto the open subset
$\varphi(M)\subseteq M'$ and therefore a development embedding in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c);

**(c)** if $M$ is connected and $\psi_1,\psi_2:M\to M'$ are two such
data-fixing isometric immersions, then $\psi_1=\psi_2$; in particular every
data-fixing self-isometry of a connected development is the identity of $M$.
